name: polyml
why: A serious Standard ML implementation with a REPL, an unusual functional language that is rarely seen in the wild.

brief.what_it_is: Poly/ML is a Standard ML implementation. It takes Standard ML source and runs or compiles it, with a native-code compiler on x86 (32- and 64-bit) and 64-bit ARM, and interpreted byte code on other architectures. The README says it is fully compatible with the ML97 standard since version 4.0 and avoids incompatible extensions, adding library extensions such as a thread library. The homepage advertises an interactive debugger. The Brew metadata lists the executables poly, polyc and polyimport, but I did not see those names on either page, so treat them as unverified.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a conservative, practical Standard ML implementation: it was originally written in an experimental language called Poly, and it is positioned as the preferred implementation for large projects such as Isabelle and HOL. Its stated focus is active development and unique features like multiprocessor threads.
brief.how_it_works: The thread library gives a simplified POSIX-threads-style interface modified for Standard ML and lets programs use multiple cores, and the garbage collector is parallelised. Native code generation is used on x86 and 64-bit ARM; other architectures get a byte-code interpreter that the download page says will be slower.

commands_seen.context: Run in the unpacked source directory before building; by default installs under /usr/local.
Builds Poly/ML after configure. The download page says older versions needed a separate 'make compiler' step, which is no longer necessary.
Installs the built files, per the source-release instructions.
Suggested on Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora, which do not include /usr/local/lib in the library search path.
Gets the development version from GitHub; the README warns it may change frequently and break.
Recommended before updating an existing git checkout to remove old files.

brief.install_notes: Standard route is the source tarball from https://github.com/polyml/polyml/releases, then ./configure, make, make install. Prefix defaults to /usr/local; some Linux distributions need --prefix=/usr. Native compiler is built on x86 and 64-bit ARM only. The download page says a 64-bit Windows binary distribution 'will follow shortly', so no Windows binary was confirmed there. No accounts or runtimes are mentioned. The brew entry itself was not described on the pages I read.
brief.standout: Poly/ML is a Standard ML system that started life as its own experimental language called Poly, and it is one of the few SML implementations that advertises parallel garbage collection and multicore threads. The 'preferred implementation for large projects' claim around Isabelle and HOL is its most concrete selling point. The scout note calls SML rare, which is an editorial claim and not from the README.
brief.status: Maintained, with partial evidence. The homepage announces that version 5.9.2 has been released and says it was last updated by David Matthews, but no dates appeared on the pages I read. The README describes 'active development', and the GitHub repo is linked as the development line with bug-fix branches such as fixes-5.9. I did not check commit dates.
brief.caveats: Native code only on x86 and 64-bit ARM; other platforms get a slower byte-code interpreter. Source build is the documented route on Unix-like systems. The development git version may break. The Windows binary was announced as forthcoming and I did not confirm it exists. The README makes no mention of licence, and I did not see one. Several docs pages were linked but I did not open them, so features like the FFI and Windows programming interface are only as described in the README.
quotes: Poly/ML takes a conservative approach to the Standard ML language and avoids incompatible extensions.
Preferred implementation for large projects such as Isabelle and HOL.
Note that the GIT code may change frequently and things may break.
